requirements.text: The rear combination lamp ESA sample(s) submitted for approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every rear combination lamp ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
The rear combination lamp ESA shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

When measured using the method of Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

When measured using the method of Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
When measured using the method of Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limit shall be constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

When measured using the method of Annex 8, the ESA narrowband emission limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

When measured using the method of Annex 8, the ESA narrowband emission limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
When measured using the method of Annex 8, the ESA narrowband emission limit shall be constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1.

The transient conducted emission of the ESA representative of its type on 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 and shall not exceed the maximum allowed pulse amplitudes given in Table 1 (12 V systems: +75 V / -100 V; 24 V systems: +150 V / -450 V).
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for radiated immunity per Annex 9 at the test levels given in Table 2a in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for radiated immunity per Annex 9 at no less than the minimum test levels given in Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
During the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".

The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b as described in Annex 10, with the test levels, numbers of pulses/durations and Functional Performance Status Classification given in Table 3b.

Where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA shall be tested with the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 at the test level, number of pulses and functional status classification given in Table 3a (status B for immunity related functions or ESA required to operate during engine start, C for other ESA).
The Functional Performance Status Classification as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied to the ESA for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.
The ESA shall only be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and Annex 8 without narrowband testing if it does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz.
The ESA shall only be exempted from testing for immunity to radiated disturbances (deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and Annex 9) if it has no immunity related functions.
The ESA shall only be exempted from transient conducted emission testing (deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.) if it is not switched, contains no switches or does not include an inductive load.

When a production ESA (rear combination lamp) taken from the series is checked for conformity, the measured broadband and narrowband electromagnetic disturbance levels shall not exceed the reference limits prescribed in paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 6.6.2.1. by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).

When a production ESA (rear combination lamp) taken from the series is checked for conformity, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength, expressed in Volts/m, up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.
Unless otherwise stated in Annex 7, the radiated broadband emission test of the lamp ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
During the radiated broadband emission test, the lamp ESA shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load (e.g. all LED functions — rear position, stop and reversing — energised).

The radiated broadband emission test of the lamp ESA (an ESA not involved in REESS charging mode) shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25, or alternatively in an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4.
The lamp ESA shall meet the radiated broadband emission limits of paragraph 6.5. of the Regulation throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz when measured in an ALSE or OATS.

When the radiated broadband emissions of the lamp ESA are measured with a peak detector, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied against the quasi-peak limits of paragraph 6.5. of the Regulation.
Unless otherwise stated in Annex 8, the radiated narrowband emission test of the lamp ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
During the radiated narrowband emission test, the lamp ESA shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
The radiated narrowband emission test of the lamp ESA shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25, or alternatively in an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4.
The lamp ESA shall meet the radiated narrowband emission limits of paragraph 6.6. of the Regulation throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz when measured in an ALSE or OATS.
The radiated narrowband emissions of the lamp ESA shall be measured with an average detector for comparison with the narrowband limits.

The lamp ESA shall comply with the immunity requirements using any combination of the absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell test (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection test (ISO 11452-4), stripline test (ISO 11452-5) or reverberation chamber test (ISO 11452-11), provided that the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9 is covered, with frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.
The immunity test conditions for the lamp ESA shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
During the immunity tests, the lamp ESA shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
The lamp ESA shall be immunity tested in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps and dwell times according to ISO 11452-1.

In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal applied to the lamp ESA shall be AM with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal applied to the lamp ESA shall be PM2 pulse modulation with Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the immunity test signal applied to the lamp ESA shall be PM3 pulse modulation with Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
When the absorber chamber test is used, the lamp ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-2 using the substitution method with vertical polarization.
When TEM cell testing is used, the lamp ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-3.

When bulk current injection testing is used, the lamp ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-4 with either the substitution method and the injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA, or the closed loop method and the injection probe at 900 mm from the ESA, or alternatively installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4 with the substitution method and probe at 150 mm.
When stripline testing is used, the lamp ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-5.
When the reverberation chamber test is used, the lamp ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-11 using a test setup with ground plane, unless otherwise specified.
The rear combination lamp ESA (LED modules, driver PCB and connector) shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply, as tested by the method of Annex 10.
The rear combination lamp ESA shall limit the conducted transients it puts onto the vehicle power supply, as tested by the method of Annex 10.

The rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 3a according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand test pulse 3b according to ISO 7637-2, applied to the 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

Unless the lamp ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2, applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The transient conducted disturbances that the rear combination lamp ESA generates on the 12/24 V supply lines and on other connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 and shall meet the applicable emission limits.

Where the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp form one unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, each of these lamps shall satisfy the provisions of this Regulation or of another Regulation (e.g. UN R150 for the retro-reflector).
The rear combination lamp unit shall not include any lamp that does not satisfy the provisions of this Regulation or of another applicable Regulation.
The rear combination lamp shall have a space large enough for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the rear combination lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking on the rear combination lamp shall have a dimension "a" of at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2., and this number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
Where the approval marking of the rear position lamp includes an arrow, the arrow shall point outwards from the vehicle.
Where the reversing lamp has the reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the arrow in its approval marking shall point outwards from the vehicle.
The rear combination lamp shall bear the approval marking.
The rear combination lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

Where the rear combination lamp uses replaceable light sources, the lamp shall be marked with the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed and, if approved for LED substitute light sources, also with the category or categories of those LED substitute light sources.

Because the rear combination lamp has non-replaceable light sources (and, where fitted, an electronic light source control gear, variable luminous intensity control or secondary operating mode), the lamp shall be marked with the rated voltage(s) (6 V, 12 V or 24 V) or the voltage range.

In case replaceable light source modules are used, each light source module shall be marked with the trade name or mark of the applicant, with the specific identification code beginning with "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle (plus additional symbols where several non-identical modules are used), and with the rated voltage(s) or voltage range.
In case replaceable light source modules are used, the rear combination lamp shall be marked with the specific identification code of the module and with the rated voltage(s) or voltage range.

Where an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, that control gear shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.

The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the rear combination lamp that is not designed to be separated from the transparent light-emitting part of the lamp.

The approval marking (and any prescribed LED substitute light source categories) shall be visible when the rear combination lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens is designed to be separated from the housing, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the housing.
Where the outer lens is shared by several devices bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings of paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5.(b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the rear combination lamp.
In case replaceable light source modules are used, the markings of paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the light source module itself.

Where a single approval mark is used, the components of that mark shall be no smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval was granted.
The rear combination lamp shall conform to the requirements of paragraphs 4. and 5. of this Regulation.

The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall meet the requirements of sections 5 and 6 of UN Regulation No. 48 (series in force at application) that apply to each lamp and to vehicle category M1, where these can be verified at lamp type approval.

The rear combination lamp shall be designed and built so that, in normal conditions of use and despite vibration, it keeps operating satisfactorily and keeps the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources or be intended for use on a vehicle with a tell-tale indicating failure of the lamps.

Where the rear position lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the logo shall be only the brand-name logo of the vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer, and all requirements for the function shall still be met.

Where the rear position lamp incorporates a logo, the enclosed light-emitting surface of the logo (transparent and non-transparent parts) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm².
The stop lamp and the reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
In the rear combination lamp, a group of LEDs wired so that failure of any one of them makes all of them stop emitting light shall be treated as one light source.

When any one light source of the rear position lamp or stop lamp fails, the lamp shall either still meet the minimum intensity of the pertinent Annex 3 standard light distribution (without exceeding the maximum intensities with all sources lit), or produce a signal to activate a failure tell-tale as in UN R48.

Where the rear position lamp is category R2 emitting more than the R1 maximum, if its variable intensity control fails the lamp shall automatically meet the steady luminous intensity requirements of its category.

Where the stop lamp is category S2 (or S4) emitting more than the maximum of category S1 (or S3), if its variable intensity control fails the lamp shall automatically meet the steady luminous intensity requirements of its category.

The rear combination lamp shall be equipped only with replaceable light sources approved under UN R37, R99 and/or R128 (with no restriction on use), light source modules and/or non-replaceable light sources.
In case of replaceable UN approved light sources, the lamp shall be designed so that the light source can be fixed only in the correct position.

In case of replaceable UN approved light sources, the light source holder shall conform to the IEC 60061 holder data sheet for the prescribed light source category (and for any prescribed LED substitute light source category).
The rear combination lamp and its LED drive electronics shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances that cause other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle to malfunction.
In case of replaceable light source modules, each module shall fit only in its designated and correct position and shall be removable only with tools.
In case of replaceable light source modules, each module shall be tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source modules, regardless of tool use, each module shall not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source or with any other module of different characteristics in the same lamp housing.
In case of replaceable light source modules, the lamp shall still meet the photometric requirements when a module is replaced by another module from the applicant with the same identification code.
Because the rear combination lamp has non-replaceable LED light sources, it shall meet all photometric and colorimetric requirements when measured with its own light sources present in the lamp.

Where the lamp may be installed in more than one position or in a field of positions, it shall meet the photometric requirements in each position or at the extreme positions of the reference axis field specified by the manufacturer.
Unless otherwise specified, the rear position, stop and reversing lamps shall meet the intensity requirements with the light source continuously lit.
An intensity requirement for a direction of observation shall be considered met if it is met in a direction deviating by no more than one-quarter of a degree from that direction.
Unless otherwise specified, the rear combination lamp shall meet the requirements with a supply voltage at the lamp of 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems).
Where the lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, it shall meet the requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.

Where the lamp with non-replaceable light sources is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, it shall meet the requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.
The intensity of each of the two samples of each function shall be at least the minimum in the pertinent function table of paragraph 5 on the reference axis (HV).
The intensity of each sample shall not exceed the maximum in the pertinent function table of paragraph 5 in any direction where the lamp is visible.

Outside the reference axis, the intensity of each sample shall be at least the minimum of paragraph 5 multiplied by the percentage given in the pertinent Annex 3 light distribution figure, or at least the intensity value given in that figure, for each direction.
Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, the intensity of each sample shall be at least the minimum in the pertinent function table of paragraph 5.
The rear position, stop and reversing lamps shall comply with the provisions of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity.
Where the rear position lamp or stop lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D", the assembly shall meet the maximum intensity with all lamps lit.
Where the rear position lamp or stop lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked "D", the assembly shall meet the minimum intensity when either lamp has failed.
Where the rear position lamp or stop lamp is an interdependent lamp system (marked "Y"), the system shall meet the requirements with all its interdependent lamps operated together.

Where the rear position lamp interdependent system is partly on a fixed and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s), and shall still meet the photometric values of the light distribution field for the inboard requirement.
Where a variable intensity control is used, it shall not generate signals that cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.

Where a variable intensity control is used, it shall not generate signals that cause luminous intensities above the steady luminous intensity maximum of paragraph 5: under night-time conditions for systems depending only on day/night conditions, and under standard conditions for other systems.

Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the ratio between the intensity with both lit and the intensity of the rear position lamp alone shall be at least 5:1 within ±5° V and ±10° H of the light distribution table, with all sources in operation where a lamp has several light sources treated as a single lamp.
The rear position, stop and reversing lamps shall meet the luminous intensity compliance tests of Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted by each function of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamp) shall meet the colorimetric requirements inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for that function in Annex 3, when tested according to the procedure described in paragraph 4.8.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid of each function, the rear combination lamp shall show no sharp variation of colour.

Because the rear combination lamp uses non-replaceable LED light sources, its colorimetric characteristics shall be verified with the LED light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.

Where a function of the rear combination lamp uses different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics of that function shall be checked for each light source technology separately according to paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.

The light emitted by the rear position lamp (category R1 steady or R2 variable) of each of the two samples supplied shall meet the minimum and maximum luminous intensities, standard light distribution (Figure A3-I) and minimum intensity within the angles of geometric visibility (Table A2-1) given in Table 4.

Where the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane shall not exceed 6.0∙10^1 cd.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.

The light emitted by the stop lamp (category S1 steady or S2 variable) of each of the two samples supplied shall meet the minimum and maximum luminous intensities, standard light distribution (Figure A3-I) and minimum intensity within the angles of geometric visibility (Table A2-1) given in Table 7.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.

The light emitted by the reversing lamp (category AR) of each of the two samples supplied shall meet the minimum luminous intensity, the maximum luminous intensities in or above the H-plane, below the H-plane down to 5°D and below 5°D, and the standard light distribution (Figure A3-V) given in Table 10.

Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices and its photometry is verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, the reversing lamp shall provide a luminous intensity of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd at that angle.
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.

In conformity of production checks, no measured value of the rear position lamp, stop lamp or reversing lamp shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation.
For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values of production lamps shall correspond to the 20 and 30 per cent values shown in Table 12.

The rear position lamp (category R1/R2) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard, reduced to 20° inboard / 80° outboard only below the H-plane where the lamp is mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.

The rear position lamp (category R1/R2) shall provide minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below, or 15° above and 5° below where the lamp is installed with its H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.

The stop lamp (category S1/S2) shall provide minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard, reduced to 20° inboard / 45° outboard only below the H-plane where the lamp is mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.

The stop lamp (category S1/S2) shall provide minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below, or 15° above and 5° below where the lamp is installed with its H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm.

The rear position lamp and stop lamp shall meet, in each direction of measurement relative to the reference axis (H = 0°, V = 0°), the minimum intensities given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Figures A3-I to A3-XV, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.

When the rear position lamp or stop lamp (S1, S2) is intended to be installed with its H-plane at a mounting height equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the light intensity of the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown on the grid lines surrounding that direction as a percentage.

When visual examination of the reversing lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions.
The rear position lamp and stop lamp shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, giving minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Tables 3 and 7.
The reversing lamp shall meet, at the measuring points of Figure A3-V relative to the axis of reference, the minimum intensities in cd shown in Figure A3-V.
The LED reversing lamp shall comply with the minimum and maximum luminous intensity requirements when measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation.

The LED rear position lamp and stop lamp shall comply with the minimum and maximum luminous intensity requirements when measured after 1 minute and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred.

Where a function does not use LED technology only, the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall comply with the luminous intensity requirements at the points in time after switch-on listed in Table A8-1 (rear position 4 s, stop 0.2 s, reversing 0.2 s, reference coordinate HV).

The retro-reflector shall have a space of sufficient size for either the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement or the approval marking, together with the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible and indelible.

When the approval marking is used, it shall include the four to six-digit sequential number of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2., and this number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
Where the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark on the retro-reflector shall follow the format of Figure I.
The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

Where such an indication is needed to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer, the Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface.
The approval marking or Unique Identifier and the markings required by paragraph 3.3.4. shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflector.

Where a single approval mark is used for the combined lamp, the size of each component of that mark shall be at least the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the relevant UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

In conformity of production checks, the mean photometric value of five specimens of the retro-reflector taken at random shall not deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The retro-reflector shall meet the requirements of sections 5 ("General specifications") and 6 ("Individual specifications") of UN Regulation No. 48 and the Annexes referenced there, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application, that apply to the rear retro-reflector and to M1 vehicles, where these can be verified at device type approval.
The retro-reflector shall be constructed so that it functions satisfactorily and continues to do so in normal use.
The retro-reflector shall have no defect in design or manufacture that harms its efficient operation or its maintenance in good condition.
The components of the retro-reflector, or parts of them, shall not be easy to dismantle.
The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean, shall not be rough, and any protuberances shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector in normal use.
Where the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, the unit and filter shall be designed so that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
The retro-reflecting optical unit and filter of the retro-reflector shall not be coloured with paint or varnish.

When the retro-reflector is illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if this gives a colourless surface reflection, the angle specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1.), the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the night-time red limits defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., the Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall meet the dimension and shape requirements of Annex 5.
When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., the Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.
When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., the Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements of paragraph 5.1.7. that apply to its materials and construction.

The retro-reflector samples shall pass the heat resistance test of Part 1 of Annex 6. At least one hour after this test, they shall still meet the colorimetric requirements of paragraph 5.1.5. and the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4. at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if necessary, in the positions defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.).
The retro-reflector shall pass the water penetration test (Annex 6) and, after it, the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
The retro-reflector shall pass the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 where this test is necessary, and the abrasive-strength test of its rear face in Part 5 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector shall pass the test for stability in time of optical properties in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The retro-reflector shall pass the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6.
After the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each test group shall have a colour that meets paragraph 5.1.5.

After the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each test group shall have an RI that meets paragraph 5.1.4., verified at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
The manufacturer shall specify one or more reference axes, or a range of them, for the retro-reflector, corresponding to the illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the RI table.

Where more than one reference axis, or a range of them, is specified, the retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements for each specified reference axis, or for the extreme axes of the specified range.
The illuminating surface of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector used for photometric measurements shall lie within a circle of 200 mm diameter.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector used for photometric measurements shall be limited to 100 cm2.
The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the illuminating surface of the retro-reflector to be used for photometric measurements.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall have RI values at least equal to the minimum values for Class IA/IB red in Table 3 (mcd·lx-1) at the angles of divergence and illumination given there.

Within the solid angle that has the centre of reference as its apex and is bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°), the retro-reflector shall not have RI values lower than those in the last two applicable columns of Table 3.
Where the Class IA/IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be met at least up to an angle of 5° downwards.
The night-time colour of the retro-reflector shall be tested by the method in paragraph 4.2.1.
The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the night-time red limits specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

The Class IA/IB retro-reflector samples shall pass the test sequence of Table 4 in chronological order, including heat (48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C with no distortion), water, motor fuels, oils, corrosion, rear face, stability in time and weathering. After each step they shall still meet the colorimetry and photometry requirements (20' and β1 = β2 = 0°).
When the RI of the rear retro-reflector is measured at β1 = β2 = 0° and slightly turning the device shows a mirror effect, the RI reading shall be taken at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.

Where the rear retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", its RI in the position of minimum RI, at an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation) and a divergence angle of 20', shall conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.

Where the rear retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", the RI at the other illumination and divergence angles shall meet the specified values in the position corresponding to the minimum-RI value of ε, or within a rotation of ±5° about the axis of reference from that position.

Where the rear retro-reflector is marked "TOP", its RI at an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation) and a divergence angle of 20' shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position during rotation of ±5° about its axis.

When the RI of the rear retro-reflector at β1 = β2 = 0° and ε = 0° exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, the rear retro-reflector shall meet the RI values for all angles of illumination and divergence measured at ε = 0°.

The rear retro-reflector shall meet the retro-reflection requirements when illuminated with CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.

The shape of the illuminating surface of the Class IA or IB rear retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for retro-reflectors of Classes IIIA and IIIB from an observation distance of 10 metres.
The moulded plastics rear retro-reflector shall withstand being kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the rear retro-reflector, and in particular of its optical component, shall be visible.

The rear retro-reflector integrated in the lamp, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface, repeated after turning through 180° with the rear face covered by about 20 mm of water, followed immediately by immersion under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.
After the water immersion test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit of the rear retro-reflector.

When visual inspection after the water immersion test does not reveal water, or in case of doubt, the rear retro-reflector, after being lightly shaken to remove excess water, shall meet the RI requirement measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

Where the rear retro-reflector is of Class IB and the manufacturer requests the alternative procedure, the rear retro-reflector shall pass the moisture and dust tests of Part 3 of Annex 6 instead of the water immersion test.
In case of the alternative moisture test, the rear retro-reflector shall be tested at a water spray precipitation rate of 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min at the device.
In case of the alternative moisture test, the lamp with the rear retro-reflector shall be tested with all drain holes and other openings open and with any drain wicks fitted in the device.
In case of the alternative moisture test, the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1 during the water spray.

In case of the alternative moisture test, the rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions grouped or reciprocally incorporated with the retro-reflector shall be operated at design voltage in a cycle of 5 min ON and 55 min OFF.
In case of the alternative moisture test, the water spray test of the device shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
In case of the alternative moisture test, the device shall be allowed to drain for 1 hour with rotation and spray off and the cabinet door closed before evaluation.
After the alternative moisture test and drain period, no standing pool of water shall be present in the interior of the device or be formable by tapping or tilting the device.
After the alternative moisture test, the rear retro-reflector, with its exterior dried with a dry cotton cloth, shall have its RI measured according to Part 1 of Annex 4.
In case of the alternative dust test, the device shall be exposed to test dust of fine powdered cement in accordance with ASTM C 150-84.
In case of the alternative dust test, the device shall be tested with all drain holes and other openings open and with any drain wicks fitted in the device.
In case of the alternative dust test, the device shall withstand dust exposure with agitation for 2 to 15 s at 15 min intervals over a duration of 5 hours.

The rear retro-reflector shall be designed so that it retains the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed, and the resistance of its front surface to tarnishing and of the protection of its rear face to deterioration shall be verified according to ISO Standard 9227:2017.

For the corrosion test, the rear combination lamp incorporating the retro-reflector shall be stripped of all removable parts and withstand a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two exposure periods of 24 hours each separated by a two-hour drying interval.

Where the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the retro-reflector shall withstand a saline mist produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the retro-reflector sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

After the corrosion test, a recovery period of 48 hours and cleaning of salt deposits, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, measured at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.

Where the moulded plastics Class IA/IB retro-reflector is mirror-backed with an accessible rear face, the brushed rear face shall withstand application for one minute of a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7, followed by drying, re-brushing and RI measurement per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. with the rear face covered in Indian ink.
The retro-reflector samples shall withstand accelerated artificial weathering in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1 for a period of 500 hours.

The outer surface of the retro-reflector, in particular the illuminating surface, shall withstand being lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol.
About five minutes after the fuel wipe, the surface of the retro-reflector shall not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks are not objected to.

The outer surface of the moulded plastics Class IA/IB retro-reflector, in particular the illuminating surface, shall withstand being lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil, and after about 5 minutes and cleaning the RI shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2.

The rear combination lamp (rear position, stop, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector) shall be so fitted that, under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
The rear combination lamp and its mounting interface shall be designed so that it is not possible for the lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.

When fitted to the vehicle, the reference axis of each light-signalling function of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, rear retro-reflector) shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

When fitted to the vehicle, the reference axis of each light-signalling function of the rear combination lamp shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
The rear combination lamp shall be fitted in compliance with any specific fitting instructions laid down by the manufacturer.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the rear combination lamp shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

In the absence of specific instructions, the left and right rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface.

In the absence of specific instructions, the left and right rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane, except with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, the left and right rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, the left and right rear combination lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics.

In case the rear combination lamps incorporate a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo shall be fitted on the rear of the vehicle, and any logo shall be a vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logo.
Where the vehicle's external shape is asymmetrical, the pair requirements of paragraph 5.5. shall be satisfied by the rear combination lamps so far as is possible.

The grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated functions of the rear combination lamp shall each fulfil all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any.

The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each function of the rear combination lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

When the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other functions (e.g. the stop lamp) which can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamp are switched ON.
The stop lamp shall not be reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator lamp.

Where a single lamp function of the rear combination lamp (as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1.(a)) has an apparent surface composed of two or more distinct parts, either (a) the total projected area of the distinct parts in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest circumscribing quadrilateral, or (b) the minimum distance between facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts shall not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicularly to the reference axis; this does not apply to a single retro-reflector.

Where a function is provided by two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro-reflectors (paragraph 2.4.11.1.(b) or (c)), either (a) the projection of their apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest circumscribing quadrilateral, or (b) the minimum distance between facing edges of the apparent surfaces shall not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Where a function of the rear combination lamp is a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(d) (interdependent lamp system), it shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
Where the rear lamps are two or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip, they shall be placed symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
Where the rear lamps are in the shape of a band or strip, they shall extend on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Where the rear lamps are in the shape of a band or strip, they shall be not less than 0.8 m long.
Where the rear lamps are in the shape of a band or strip, the illumination of the band surface shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends.

Where the light-emitting surface of a band or strip lamp is constituted by juxtaposed elements, the individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

The maximum mounting height of each function of the rear combination lamp shall be determined from the highest point, and the minimum height from the lowest point, of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the height above the ground of each function of the rear combination lamp shall be measured from the H plane.

The position in width of each function of the rear combination lamp shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface furthest from the median longitudinal plane when referred to overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface when referred to the distance between lamps.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall not be intentionally varied while the lamp is switched ON.

When the photometric characteristics of a function of the rear combination lamp vary in relation to ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp provides another lighting function, the variation shall comply with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by the rear position lamp, stop lamp and rear retro-reflector shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red rear position lamp or stop lamp when viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front by the rear combination lamp, as verified during type approval of the lamp and taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable, shall be not more than 0.25 cd per lamp.

The electrical connections of the rear position lamps shall be such that they can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps, the end-outline and side-marker lamps if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp, except under the conditions listed in paragraph 5.11.1. (e.g. use as parking lamps).
In case a function of the rear combination lamp is an interdependent lamp system, all its light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector shall not be concealable.
The light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall be red.

The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
Where any function of the rear combination lamp is installed on a movable component, the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. shall be fulfilled.

Where the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector is installed on a movable component, it shall meet all position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component.

Where the rear position lamp function is obtained by an assembly of two lamps marked "D" on a movable component, at least one of the lamps shall meet the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component.

Where additional rear position lamps or rear retro-reflectors are switched ON/used when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

Where the rear position lamp is an interdependent lamp system mounted completely on a movable component, it shall satisfy paragraph 5.18.1., and any additional lamps switched ON in a fixed open position shall satisfy all position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps on the movable component.

Where the rear position lamp is an interdependent lamp system mounted partly on the fixed and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant during device approval shall meet all position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component, and inwards geometric visibility is deemed satisfied only if they still conform to the photometric values in the field of light distribution at all those positions.

When the rear combination lamp is installed on a movable component (e.g. tailgate) and the movable component is in a position other than a "normal position of use", the lamp shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.

When the rear combination lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp and of the rear retro-reflector shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".

Where the 50 per cent limit of paragraph 5.21. is not practicable for the rear position lamp, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

The rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions shall be operable without anything more than the installation of a light source and/or a fuse; otherwise the lamp is deemed not to be present (this does not apply to the retro-reflector).

In case the lamp is approved with replaceable light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37 (not used as non-replaceable light sources as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2.), the lamp shall be fitted so that the light source can be correctly replaced without expert assistance and without special tools other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

In case a light source module of the lamp includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to UN Regulation No. 37, that light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.

Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp light-signalling function is provided, the replacement function shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function is provided, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.

Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function is provided, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5.) shall indicate, during replacement, the occurrence of a temporary replacement and the need for repair.

Where the rear position lamp (category R2) and the stop lamp (category S2) have variable luminous intensity control and are combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, the intensities of all these lamps shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

Where the R2 rear position lamp and S2 stop lamp have variable luminous intensity control, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of the two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions in the entire intensity range.

Where the R2 rear position lamp or S2 stop lamp has variable luminous intensity, intensity increase and decrease in relation to environmental conditions shall only respond to ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds or contamination of the light emitting surface, and shall stay within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations.

Where the R2 rear position lamp or S2 stop lamp has variable luminous intensity, a traffic-related decrease of luminous intensity shall only be activated while the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal to or less than 20 m, shall stay within the limits of the pertinent UN Regulations, and may remain active only as long as the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 50 km/h.
Where the rear position lamp or stop lamp has variable luminous intensity, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition.

When the vehicle electrical system is in a constant voltage operating condition and the lamp functions have been approved with a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, the voltage at the lamp terminals shall not exceed the voltage specified for those functions as approved (not applicable to devices covered by paragraph 5.27.3.).

In all power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the lamp terminals shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) by more than 3 per cent, unless the lamp includes an electronic light source control gear, an integral variable intensity control, or only UN R128 light sources (paragraph 5.27.3.).

There shall be no obstacle inside the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of each lamp function observed from infinity, except obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved.

When any part of the apparent surface of the installed lamp is hidden by further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
In case any lamp function is an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector shall be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations (UN R148 for the lamps, UN R150 for the retro-reflector) as specified in paragraph 6.
In case the light-signalling lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

In case the lamp is approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128, it shall be fitted with light sources approved according to those categories only (not applicable to LED modules and non-replaceable light sources unless required to be approved).

In case the lamp is approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s), it shall only be used where the statement in paragraph 3.2.8. is present and positive, and the lamp shall bear the marking related to the use of LED substitute light source(s).
On an M1 vehicle, one reversing lamp device shall be installed, and no more than one additional (second) reversing lamp device shall be installed as an option.
The reversing lamp shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be installed not less than 250 mm above the ground.
The reversing lamp shall be installed not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
The reversing lamp shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle in length.
The reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle shall provide geometric visibility, defined by angle α as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., of 15° upwards and 5° downwards.

When only one reversing lamp device is installed at the rear, the reversing lamp shall provide geometric visibility, defined by angle β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., of 45° to the right and to the left.

When two reversing lamp devices are installed at the rear, each reversing lamp shall provide geometric visibility, defined by angle β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., of 45° outwards and 30° inwards.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in a position in which operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the propulsion system start/stop control is not in a position in which operation of the propulsion system is possible.
Where the component regulation (UN R23 or UN R148) requires it, a tell-tale indicating failure of the reversing lamp shall be provided.
The vehicle shall be fitted with two S1 or S2 category stop lamps, of which the product provides one per side.
The stop lamp shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

On M1 vehicles, the point on the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 category stop lamp in the direction of the reference axis that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be mounted not less than 350 mm above the ground.

The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be mounted not more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).

The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be positioned so that the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of its apparent surface is below the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface of the S3 or S4 category stop lamp.
The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall be located at the rear of the vehicle.
The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.

When the S1 or S2 category stop lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of geometric visibility shall be not less than 20° under the H plane.
The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal.
Where the S1 or S2 category stop lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of geometric visibility shall be not less than 5°.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
Where the component regulation requires it, a tell-tale indicating failure of the stop lamp shall be provided.

The vehicle shall be fitted with two rear position lamps, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The point on the apparent surface of the rear position lamp in the direction of the reference axis that is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The rear position lamp shall be mounted not less than 350 mm above the ground.

The rear position lamp shall be mounted not more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
The rear position lamp shall be located at the rear of the vehicle.
The rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° inwards and 80° outwards.
Where the rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal angle of geometric visibility shall be not less than 20° under the H plane.
The rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal.
Where the rear position lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of geometric visibility shall be not less than 5°.

When, on an M1 vehicle fitted with a rear side-marker lamp, the manufacturer chooses the alternative of paragraph 6.10.5.2., the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° outwards to 45° inwards (inward angle not less than 20° under the H plane where mounted below 750 mm).

When the alternative of paragraph 6.10.5.2. is used, the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal (downward angle not less than 5° where mounted below 750 mm).

When the alternative of paragraph 6.10.5.2. is used, the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of at least 12.5 square centimetres of apparent surface within the visibility angles, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
The electrical connections of the rear position lamp shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.
The rear position lamps shall have a closed-circuit tell-tale combined with that of the front position lamps, except while daytime running lamps are switched ON.
Where the component Regulation requires it, a tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamp shall be provided.
Where a rear fog lamp is installed, the distance between the rear fog lamp and each stop lamp shall be greater than 100 mm.

Where the parking lamp function is performed by the rear position lamps according to paragraph 6.12.9., the rear position lamps shall be able to operate even if the device which starts the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
Where the parking lamp function is performed by the rear position lamps, no device shall automatically switch these lamps OFF as a function of time.

The rear retro-reflectors (two per vehicle) shall be type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.
Where additional retro-reflecting devices or materials are fitted in the rear combination lamp, they shall not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

The point on the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The rear retro-reflector shall be mounted not less than 250 mm above the ground.

When grouped with any rear lamp(s), the rear retro-reflector shall be mounted not more than 1,200 mm above the ground (not more than 900 mm if not grouped), or not more than 1,500 mm above the ground only if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively.
The rear retro-reflector shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.
The rear retro-reflector shall provide geometric visibility over a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and 30° outwards.
The rear retro-reflector shall provide geometric visibility over a vertical angle of 10° above the horizontal.
The rear retro-reflector shall provide geometric visibility over a vertical angle of 10° below the horizontal.

Where the rear retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the rear retro-reflector shall provide geometric visibility of at least 5° below the horizontal instead of 10°.

When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON, except that the rear position lamps may be switched OFF and remain OFF only as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to Annex 13).

When the check under paragraph 5.10.4. is made that the red light of the rear position lamps, stop lamps and rear retro-reflector cannot be seen from the front, the zone explored by the observer's eye shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground.

When the check under paragraph 5.10.4. is made that the red light of the rear combination lamp cannot be seen from the front, the zone explored by the observer's eye shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes forming an angle of 15° outwards to the front from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, passing through the point(s) of contact of vertical planes parallel to the median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width, the foremost point of contact corresponding to the forward plane.
